name: Eugene F. Douglass
office: U.S. House, North Carolina 2nd Congressional District, 2026
profileSummary: Serial Republican candidate (since 1998, never elected) and retired chemistry professor running on three explicit pillars: abolish the Department of Education, protect life from conception, and shrink the federal government. No legislative record; positions are highly consistent across 25+ years of candidacies.

Protect life from conception to natural death; opposes all public funding for abortion
Small federal government, lower taxes, balanced budget amendment, less regulation
GRNC-PVF 96% rating and four-star recommendation on firearms
Strict immigration enforcement: immediate deportation, border wall, end sanctuary cities

His Judeo-Christian ethical framework and 'no compromise on moral values' stance indicate strong opposition to government health mandates that conflict with religious values. tradition.reasoning: Tradition is the most defining value in Douglass's public identity. He explicitly grounds his positions in 'the Judaeo-Christian ethic of our country as described in the Declaration of Independence and our US Constitution.' He states 'no compromise on moral values.' His education at The King's College (conservative Christian institution) and Bethel Theological Seminary, his 'conception until natural death' framing, and his 25-year consistency across candidacies all point to tradition as the central organizing value. He attended a seminary and self-describes as 'a Christian' before any other identity.

conformity.reasoning: Strong respect for established rules and norms, especially constitutional and religious ones. His insistence on following 'our constitution' and explicit endorsement of established party platforms (2016 GOP platform 'reaffirmed each presidential election year') reflects conformity to accepted standards. His immigration position emphasizes legal process ('get in line with those trying to immigrate here legally'). However, his serial candidacy against party-favored candidates and willingness to run as an underdog shows some independent streak that moderates this score.

security.reasoning: Strong emphasis on national security through immigration enforcement (wall, deportation, more CBP agents), 'protect innocent human life,' and law-and-order orientation. His strict immigration platform is framed around safety and order. The 2016 GOP platform endorsement includes strong national defense and border security. His firearms position (GRNC 96%) frames gun ownership partly through self-defense. Security is a consistent secondary theme after tradition.

self_direction.reasoning: Some positive signal: his emphasis on individual liberty over government mandates ('monies should remain with taxpayers'), opposition to federal bureaucracy, and support for families choosing their own schools. However, this is limited by his willingness to impose moral values through law (abortion restrictions, opposition to gender-affirming care). His self-direction is economic and educational, not social. The 'no compromise on moral values' stance directly limits self-direction for others on social issues.

power.reasoning: Douglass shows no pursuit of social status, prestige, or dominance over resources. He is a perennial underdog candidate with no notable endorsements, no fundraising apparatus, no campaign website, and no institutional backing. He lost his 2024 primary with 22.5% of the vote. He operates through Substack and LinkedIn. His self-description emphasizes 'happily retired college Chemistry teacher, father and grandfather' — the opposite of a power-oriented identity. His anti-establishment positioning and decades of futile candidacies suggest power is not a motivating value.

achievement.reasoning: His academic credentials (Ph.D., multiple graduate degrees, 30+ years teaching) and persistent candidacy show some drive for personal accomplishment. However, his public identity does not emphasize personal success or competence as motivating values. His campaign framing is moral and ideological, not achievement-oriented. Weak positive signal from career accomplishments only.

universalism.reasoning: Douglass's positions actively work against universalism in several ways: opposition to safety net programs that serve all people, strict immigration enforcement that excludes undocumented immigrants from any public benefits, opposition to reproductive autonomy, and opposition to gender-affirming care framed as 'depraved eugenics ideology.' His moral framework is explicitly particularist (Judeo-Christian) rather than universal. His 'no compromise on moral values' stance prioritizes one moral tradition over pluralistic tolerance. The only universalist element is his 'protect innocent human life' framing, which extends concern to the unborn — but this is applied selectively and paired with punitive enforcement.

benevolence.reasoning: Weak positive signal. His 'protect innocent human life' pillar shows concern for in-group welfare (the unborn, children). His teaching career spanning 30+ years demonstrates sustained commitment to helping others develop. Self-describes as 'father and grandfather.' However, his benevolence is narrowly scoped — it does not extend to immigrants ('immediately deported'), people seeking abortion ('murder of an unborn child'), or transgender youth ('castration and mutilation'). The in-group boundary is tightly drawn around those who share his moral framework.

stimulation.reasoning: Douglass actively resists novelty and change. His positions have been identical for 25+ years. He explicitly opposes social changes (gender-affirming care, expanded abortion access). His 'no compromise on moral values' and constitutional originalism resist new interpretations. His endorsement of the 2016 platform 'reaffirmed each election year' emphasizes continuity over change. His teaching career at one institution for 15+ years and his consistent ideological framework suggest low openness to new experiences.

hedonism.reasoning: No evidence of pleasure-seeking or sensuous gratification as a motivating value. His evangelical Christian background and seminary education, combined with his moral absolutism on social issues, suggest restraint rather than hedonism. His self-description emphasizes duty (teaching, family, faith) over enjoyment. Mild negative signal — not actively anti-hedonist in policy terms, but personally oriented away from this value.
